title: Cajun Chicken and Rice Skillet
seoTitle: Cajun Chicken and Rice Skillet | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: One-skillet spiced chicken with peppers and rice for ten
subtitle: One-skillet spiced chicken with peppers and rice for ten
description: Chicken thighs are seared with Cajun seasoning, then simmered with trinity vegetables, rice, and broth until fluffy and fragrant. Finish with scallions and hot sauce at the line.
equipment: Large cast iron skillet or Dutch oven

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Cajun Chicken and Rice Skillet in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Season and sear chicken
steps.instruction: Toss chicken thighs with half the Cajun seasoning. Sear skin-side down in a large skillet over medium-high heat 5 minutes per side until golden. Set aside.

steps.title: Cook the trinity
steps.instruction: In the same pan, sauté onion, bell pepper, celery, and garlic 6–8 minutes until softened and lightly caramelized at the edges. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Toast rice and build
steps.instruction: Stir in rice and remaining Cajun seasoning, toast 2 minutes, then add tomato paste and broth. Nestle seared chicken skin-side up into the rice.

steps.title: Simmer covered
steps.instruction: Cover and simmer on low 25–30 minutes until rice absorbs liquid and chicken reaches 165°F internal. Avoid stirring so rice stays fluffy.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Cajun Chicken and Rice Skillet onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 10 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.instruction: Rest covered 5 minutes off heat. Fluff rice gently around chicken, scatter green onions, and serve straight from the skillet or transfer to a hotel pan.

steps.title: Final quality check before service
steps.instruction: Walk the line once before opening service for Cajun Chicken and Rice Skillet — confirm hotel pans are labeled, backup trays are in the 200°F oven, and thermometers are calibrated. Rookies should ask a senior cook to spot-check the first portion.

proTips: If rice looks dry before chicken finishes, add broth ¼ cup at a time—not water.
Andouille sausage slices stirred in at step 2 add smoke without extra pans.
A tight-fitting lid or foil seal is critical—steam escapes and rice stays crunchy.
tonightSpread: Skillet served with cornbread muffins and extra hot sauce on the side.
Simple iceberg salad with ranch for crew who want something cool.
leftovers: Reheat covered with splash of broth for lunch bowls the next day.
Stuff into bell pepper halves and bake for a quick round-two dinner.
whyCrewsLikeIt: One pan means fewer dishes after a busy day. Bold Cajun flavor reads as a proper meal, not a rookie rice packet, and the skillet format holds warm on the stove between calls.
mealPrepNotes: Dice trinity uniform so it cooks evenly. Use a large cast iron or hotel pan for ten portions. Keep hot sauce off to the side for heat-sensitive crew.
